text:
Ryan Chen: hi @jamie_people_ops — I need to request a temporary ADA accommodation. I have panic disorder flares tied to late-night oncall. Can we reduce my oncall load for ~3 months and get hybrid-only shifts?

Jamie (People Ops): thanks for flagging this, Ryan. sorry you're dealing with this. we can start the interactive process. can you DM me a short note and upload any medical documentation when you’re ready? we’ll keep it confidential. :heart:

Ryan Chen: DM'd a quick note. have a doc from my provider but need to confirm what level of detail is required. also worried about performance flags from last sprint — don’t want this to make things worse.

Sana Patel: @ryan chen I saw the note. safety first — we'll cover you. can you outline which oncall tasks are most trigger-y? night alerts or pager escalations?

Ryan Chen: night alerts and the overnight rotation. daytime pages fine. panic attacks usually after 11pm.

Alex M: I can swap some of Ryan's overnight shifts for the next 6 weeks. happy to help. :thumbsup:

Jamie (People Ops): rough plan: 1) collect provider note (high-level is fine: diagnosis + recommended limitations), 2) one-hour interactive meeting w/ you + manager + people-ops to define accommodations, 3) temporary adjustments doc + review in 30 days.

Sana Patel: propose temporary adjustments:
```
- exempt from 11pm-7am oncall for 12 weeks
- daytime oncall only, or shorter shifts (8am-8pm)
- buddy coverage for critical overnight pager escalations
- weekly 1:1 check-in with manager
```
We can add training for the buddy on your services.

Ryan Chen: that looks reasonable. I appreciate Alex jumping in. confidentiality is important — please limit notes to the team in the meeting.

Jamie (People Ops): absolutely — accommodation details will be on a need-to-know basis. HR Bot: scheduling poll created: "Interactive Accom Meeting — Ryan" — use /pick to choose times.

HR Bot: meeting created for 1998765480, 1998765540, 1998765600 — vote to confirm.

Alex M: voted for 1998765540.

Sana Patel: noted the recent performance incident in private. we'll separate that from accommodation paperwork — but we will set clear temporary performance expectations so no surprises. main goal: keep you healthy and productive.

Ryan Chen: thank you. one question — will taking this accommodation affect career review or promo timeline?

Jamie (People Ops): it shouldn't. we’ll add a 30-day review checkpoint to assess workload and impact; promotions are based on output and impact over time, and reasonable accommodations are protected. we'll document goals and measurements for the review period.

Sana Patel: I'll draft a short coverage matrix and a 30-day success checklist after the meeting.

Ryan Chen: appreciate it all. if anyone needs docs from my provider, send me the secure link and I'll upload.

Jamie (People Ops): thanks everyone. will follow up with the confirmed meeting time and the next steps after votes. :pray:
